briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for July 25, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of Global Extreme Climate Phenomena
sections.content: Today, South Korea was hit by extreme heat approaching a daytime high of 40 degrees Celsius in various regions, leading to the rapid expansion of severe heatwave warnings. The seriousness was further exacerbated by tropical night phenomena observed in some areas of Daegu and Gyeongbuk [2, 10]. Such heatwaves are clear evidence that climate change is a reality, with the acceleration of climate change being observed globally [11, 12]. Particularly across Europe, the risk of drought is increasing due to climate change, and scientists warn that climate change is exacerbating droughts in Europe [13, 20]. In France and Spain, fierce wildfires have spread, leading to the evacuation or lockdown orders for over 200,000 people in several regions, including the outskirts of Bordeaux. Spain has declared a national emergency, facing a severe situation [21, 23, 24, 25]. In France, a regrettable situation also occurred where volunteers stepped in to rescue hundreds of fish at risk of dying due to low river levels caused by the heatwave [26].

sections.title: ⚠️ Accelerating Threats to Ecosystems and Livelihoods
sections.content: The acceleration of climate change extends beyond mere unusual weather events, posing direct threats to ecosystems and the livelihoods of local communities [12]. In the Georgia region, climate change has been confirmed to be altering the biological rhythms of wildlife, suggesting widespread ecological disruption globally [14]. Furthermore, in the Kashmir region, a serious situation is unfolding where beekeepers' livelihoods are threatened as beehives are emptying due to climate change [22]. These phenomena demonstrate that the impacts of climate change on human life and the natural environment are increasingly unpredictable and appearing in more fatal forms.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Energy Transition Policies and Market Trends
sections.content: Domestically, ongoing discussions are taking place regarding the direction of energy policy, including controversy over a minister's changing stance on renewable energy expansion [5]. Meanwhile, in the KOSPI market, the impact of international affairs on the energy market has become clear, with renewable energy-related stocks surging due to tensions in the Middle East [6]. This situation is leading to a strategic shift in South Korea's energy investment direction, prioritizing grid investment over solar power [7]. In the United States, as the construction of AI data centers faces NIMBY (Not In My Backyard) phenomena, the combination of renewable energy and Energy Storage Systems (ESS) is drawing attention as a potential new solution [9].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts to Address Climate Change
sections.content: As the sense of crisis regarding climate change intensifies, various response efforts are continuing both domestically and internationally. Namwon City has completed the maintenance of its sewage facilities in preparation for increasingly frequent heavy rainfall due to climate change, thereby enhancing its climate resilience [1]. Interest in nature-based solutions is also growing, with moss being rediscovered as a new key player in landscaping for the carbon-neutral era [3]. Sacheon City is promoting a pilot project for carbon neutrality practices targeting rural women leaders and child trainees, encouraging community participation [4], and in Yeonggwang County, a public-interest solar power project has officially commenced, contributing to the expansion of renewable energy supply [8]. Internationally, a new satellite is set to monitor climate change and volcanic activity, with expectations for strengthened response capabilities through scientific surveillance [16].

briefing.closing: This concludes today's climate briefing for July 25, 2026.
